gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: Wrap up warm, or you'll ___ a cold.
gaps.explanation: catch a cold is the fixed collocation for becoming ill with one.

gaps.sentence: Our guide was highly ___ and had climbed the mountain five times.
gaps.explanation: highly experienced is the standard collocation; 'highly' combines with participial adjectives.

gaps.sentence: I'm ___ a course in web design this term.
gaps.explanation: do a course is the British English collocation for studying on a course.

gaps.sentence: Unlike some politicians, she ___ her promises.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'promises' (she is unlike other politicians)
gaps.explanation: keep a promise means to do what you promised; the contrast with other politicians shows the positive verb.

gaps.sentence: Everyone agreed the suggestion was utterly ___.
gaps.explanation: utterly ridiculous is the standard collocation; 'utterly' is used with extreme adjectives.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the blame for the accident onto the weather.
gaps.explanation: 'Shift the blame onto somebody' = transfer responsibility.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.
